facts.raw_span: A 64-year-old white man was admitted in March 2016 with acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia
he had been on therapeutic anticoagulation for paroxysmal “pre-shimmering”
two hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV, first noted in August 2015
biopsies at that time showed histologically proven adenoma without malignancy
he was hemodynamically stable but had a hemoglobin level of 4.4 mmol/L
he reported no weight loss, fever, or constitutional symptoms
α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels within normal ranges
abdominal ultrasound revealed subcapsular hepatic bleeding
contrast-enhanced CT confirmed active bleeding from one of the two hypervascular lesions in segment IV
after angiographic embolization and conservative management, bleeding resolved
follow-up CT showed persistent hypervascular lesions without typical features of hepatocellular carcinoma
MRI demonstrated hypervascular lesions with central necrosis
